title: Make Room for Others
body:
**“In humility count others more significant than yourselves.”**

Humility does not mean pretending you have no value. It means you no longer need to make yourself the centre of every room.

Paul points to Jesus, who possessed true glory yet chose the path of service. His humility was not insecurity. It was strength placed at the service of love.

Pride asks, “How does this affect me?” Humility also asks, “What does this person need?” It listens without planning a reply, celebrates another person without comparison and serves without turning the act into a story about itself.

Make room today. Let someone finish speaking. Notice the person being overlooked. Choose not to mention your own achievement. Take the less important place without resentment.

Humility makes space for love to become practical.
